references.text: God says he will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same theme of God hardening Egypt's heart.
God hardens Pharaoh's heart and multiplies his signs and wonders in Egypt.
God says he will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites, and God will be glorified through Pharaoh.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that he pursued the Israelites with his army.
The Egyptians shall know that the Lord is God when he is glorified through Pharaoh, his chariots and horsemen.
Fulfillment of the prophecy: the Egyptians pursued the Israelites with all of Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen.
Moses' song celebrates how the Lord was glorified by casting horse and rider into the sea.
Pharaoh's chariots and army were cast into the sea, a glorification of God through Egypt's downfall.
God glorifies himself through judgment on enemies, a similar theme of divine glorification through victory.
Paul quotes about Pharaoh to show God's sovereignty in hardening hearts to display his power and glorify his name.
A direct historical reference using Pharaoh's fate in Exodus as a theological example of the consequences of hardening one's heart.
Narrative connection between the promise of signs (chap. 3) and their fulfillment at the Red Sea (chap. 14).
Theological contrast between the hardening of Pharaoh's heart (judgment) and the gift of a new heart to Israel (grace).
A direct reference to the fate of Pharaoh and his army at the Red Sea as described in Exodus.
